title: Fixed Points of a Random Permutation
summary: A video-sourced mathematical note presented in three forms: a close English reproduction, a corrected English report, and a revised Chinese report.
metaDescription: A reproduction and corrected bilingual editions of the mathematical note shown in BV1Fh411N71S.
deck: A reconstruction of the mathematical note visible in a Bilibili video, accompanied by corrected, self-contained reports in English and Chinese.
editionsIntroduction: The reproduction preserves what appeared in the video. The two revised reports repair the mathematics and exposition, and stand on their own.

editions.title: Source-faithful edition
editions.description: A close typesetting of the four visible pages, intentionally preserving their unusual wording, omissions, notation, and induction calculation.

editions.title: Corrected report
editions.description: A self-contained treatment with a precise model, an inclusion–exclusion proof, a unified probability distribution, and an indicator-variable proof of the expectation.

editions.title: 中文修订报告
editions.description: 与英文修订版内容一致的规范中文报告。该版采用相同的定义、结论与证明，并非对复刻版中不规范措辞的逐字翻译。

editorial.title: Editorial note
editorial.introduction: This publication is an independent LaTeX reproduction of, and editorial adaptation based on, the paper shown in the Bilibili video linked below. The close reproduction is distinguished from the two corrected reports throughout.

purpose.after: It is unofficial, is not presented as an author-approved transcript, and makes no claim of affiliation with the video creator or Bilibili.

source.title: 【日常研究】摆烂小能手掀起的数学问题

title: One Name, Two Sound Systems
summary: The phonology of personal names in Chinese and Japanese: Mandarin tones and finals, Japanese morae and pitch accent, and the patterns we learn to hear.
metaDescription: A bilingual essay on the phonology of personal names in Chinese and Japanese, illustrated with familiar names from anime, games, and related media.
deck: The phonology of personal names in Chinese and Japanese: what changes when the same familiar name is spoken in another language?
